title: CLI startup sequence: main.run → options applied
answers: Where are command-line option values applied?
Why is the argparse parser built after the master/addons are created?
body:
Entry: `tools/main.py:mitmproxy|mitmdump|mitmweb` lazily import tool pkg → `main.run(master_cls, make_parser, args, extra)`. Inner `main()` order:
1. `options.Options()` (core options via `add_option` in `options.py:Options.__init__`).
2. `master_cls(opts)`: `master.py:Master.__init__` creates CommandManager/AddonManager; `AddonManager.__init__` hooks `options.changed` → `_configure_all` (ConfigureHook to all addons). `DumpMaster.__init__` (`tools/dump.py`) adds `addons.default_addons()`, Dumper, KeepServing, ReadFileStdin, ErrorCheck.
3. `make_parser(opts)` AFTER addons load (parser is built from registered options), then `parse_args`; failure → `arg_check.check()`, exit 1.
4. `opts.set(*args.setoptions, defer=True)` (--set), then `optmanager.load_paths` for confdir config.yaml/yml, then `process_options` (`--version`, -q/-v tweak termlog_verbosity/flow_detail, then `opts.update(**adict)` for non-None parsed values that are `in opts`).
5. `--options`/`--commands` dump and exit; then `extra(args)` (mitmdump: filter → save_stream_filter/readfile_filter/dumper_filter) applied via `opts.update`; signal handlers; `await master.run()`.
